editorial:
You meet Tom, a quiet lighthouse keeper, and Isabel, his hopeful wife, living far from everyone on a rocky island off Western Australia. Their life feels peaceful until a rowboat washes up with a baby and a dead man inside. Instead of reporting it right away, they raise the child as their own. That choice gives them joy, but it also plants a secret that grows heavier with every year.

The movie moves slowly, but the acting is strong and the ocean views are gorgeous. It asks hard questions about love, guilt, and what makes a parent. The music and costumes also help sell the period. The downside is the sad tone and long runtime, so it is not a light watch. If you enjoy emotional dramas, this is a good pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the end, Tom confesses that Lucy is not their biological child, and he goes to prison to protect Isabel. Lucy is returned to her birth mother, Hannah, and grows up as Grace. Years later, after Tom is released, he and Isabel slowly rebuild their life. The final scenes show an older Lucy visiting them, bringing peace and forgiveness, proving love can survive even after a painful mistake.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt dramas and beautiful coastal scenery.
